title: Quadratic Strong-Operator Paving over Arbitrary Maximal Abelian Subalgebras
main_claim: Take any masa A in any von Neumann algebra M, any self-adjoint x in M, and any 0<eps<1. Then x is (eps, r_eps) strong-operator pavable over A, with r_eps = ceil(4e8 eps^-2) + ceil(4/eps) + 1 <= 5e8 eps^-2. The count is fixed before the strong neighbourhood is chosen, and neither separability nor a conditional expectation is assumed. This proves the quadratic so-paving conjecture of Popa and Vaes (PV15, Conjecture 2.8(2)).

issues.description: The initial-cost step needs the largest root of the mixed determinantal polynomial to be below 3/sqrt(r) when k=2r. This rests entirely on the cited constant 3*sqrt(2)/sqrt(k) from RS17 Theorem 25, which cannot be checked from this source. There is slack, though: t=4/sqrt(r) works as long as the true constant is below 4*sqrt(2). So only a much weaker RS17 bound would cause a problem.
issues.evidence: Equation (poly-mixed-upper) is [RS17, Theorem 25], whose hypotheses are zero-diagonal Hermitian contractions and k>=2.

issues.description: The ultrapower norm-paving corollary is a one-line appeal to the forward transfer in PV15 Theorem 2.7(3). Its hypotheses (countably decomposable, expected masa) cannot be checked against the source here. This does not affect the main theorem.
issues.evidence: The forward transfer in [PV15, Theorem 2.7(3)] gives the stated norm paving in M^omega with the same error and number of projections.

coverage:
I read all eight section files of the LaTeX source in full, and checked the main steps line by line.

- **Reductions:**
  - No-central lemma: positive-cone inequality, block-sum identity, randomized refinement variance, coloring variance (pairwise-uncorrelated indicators), Jordan overlap identity, spectral Markov bound giving 3eps/4.
  - Corner assembly: p in A, (1-p) corner has no central functional, disjoint palettes, count R + ceil(4/eps) + 1.
  - Pinching lemma and separable reduction, including the masa property of A_0.
- **Kernels:** atomless-kernel proposition (Lusin-Novikov selection, the intertwiner b in ker E_N, polar decomposition, the type I lemma turning u into a groupoid normalizer, composition of kernels, p_at y = 0).
- **Polynomials:** the differential identity, half-plane quotient bound, arrow matrix and rooted measures, endpoint lemma (weight factoring, monotonicity), tail estimate, second-moment and locality bounds. I re-derived the single-site assignment lemma in both cases and got 21m and 7m, both within the stated 24m.
- **Invariant and coloring:** the Maharam lift invariance and edge-ratio computation, bad-ball bound, hazard-step identity and error term, the recursion for S_N, the unassigned-probability bound and the symmetry argument for color marginals. I checked the argument-formula and Poisson recovery of d_v and the height-homogeneity step. I skimmed the analytic-continuation details of the rank comparison rather than re-deriving them.
- **Transfer:** freeness model, free compression bound (lambda + 2*sqrt(lambda)), reduction to centered alternating words, Fourier and inclusion-exclusion step, the same-block pair case, the shortest-pair Cauchy-Schwarz split (interior mates lie off the arc) and the coarse-to-fine collision limit.
- **Completion:** clipping via the right-multiplier algebra, the fixed-moment limit and final spectral cut. All numerical constants check out: 1280/sqrt(r) + eps/16 = 253/2000 eps; 2(1/r + 2/sqrt(r)) <= 40001/2e8 eps; r <= 400000007 eps^-2.

Two external results are taken on citation: the constant in RS17 Theorem 25, and the Ueda amalgamated free-product construction.
